ei.title: Reading1 — Psychology — Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
ei.subject: ReadingExpert5

fullPassage: What are the basic requirements of life and what do we need next after those? When you answer these questions, you’re doing the same kind of work that American psychologist Abraham Maslow did in his “hierarchy of needs” theory. The theory states that we must progress through various levels, satisfying the needs of each before being able to move on to the next. He thought individuals could eventually fulfill their potential if they could just satisfy several fundamental needs. The most basic needs form the bottom of Maslow’s hierarchy and are referred to as physiological needs. Physiological needs include our needs for food and shelter. Unless these are satisfied, we cannot move to the next level, safety needs. We need to feel secure in our environment, and this feeling of security usually means protection and freedom from fear. The third level is the need for love and belonging. People satisfy this need through their families and homes, as well as by joining and forming groups, making friends, and being part of a team. In the fourth level, the need for esteem refers to people’s need to be recognized. Here, they want to feel that others think highly of them; they may need praise and want to feel good about themselves. They may try to accomplish this by achieving set goals. Self-actualization, the fifth level, is the summit of Maslow’s hierarchy of needs. It is the quest to reach one’s full human potential. In this process people tend to have needs such as truth, justice, wisdom, and spiritual fulfillment. Despite the appealing logic of Maslow’s hierarchy, it seems to have some limits. Extensive research has suggested that there is little evidence for the ranking of levels and the argument of a definite hierarchy. Moreover, the concept of self-actualization is vague, and there’s no evidence to show that every individual can reach it. Maslow was the first psychologist to carry out academic research on human needs. He believed everybody should be encouraged to discover their vocations in life and endeavor to make life better. These are still important lessons today.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: referring → referred: 'are ______ to as'는 '~로 불린다'는 수동태라 과거분사(be + p.p.)로 써요.

det.korean: satisfied → satisfying: 분사구문에서 우리(we)가 욕구를 '충족하는' 능동 관계라 현재분사 satisfying으로 써요.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: fearful(두려워하는) → secure(안전한): 안전 욕구는 환경에서 '안전하다고' 느끼는 것이라 secure가 맞아요.
det.analysis:
① fundamental(근본적인) — 몇 가지 '근본적인' 욕구를 충족한다로 자연스러워요

② fearful(두려워하는) — 원문은 secure(안전한)예요. 안전 욕구는 환경에서 '안전하다고' 느끼는 것이라 '두려워하는'은 반대예요 ←정답(부적절)

③ praise(칭찬) — 존중 욕구에서 '칭찬'이 필요할 수 있다로 자연스러워요

④ truth(진리) — 자아실현에서 '진리' 같은 욕구를 갖는다로 자연스러워요
det.tip: feel secure in our environment = 환경에서 안전하다고 느끼다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: obvious(분명한) → vague(모호한): 자아실현 개념이 '모호하다'는 한계를 지적하는 흐름이라 vague가 맞아요.
det.analysis:
① progress(나아가다) — 여러 단계를 거쳐 '나아가야' 한다로 자연스러워요

② belonging(소속) — 사랑과 '소속'의 욕구라 자연스러워요

③ summit(정상) — 자아실현은 위계의 '정상'이라로 자연스러워요

④ obvious(분명한) — 원문은 vague(모호한)예요. 바로 뒤에서 '도달 가능하다는 증거가 없다'며 한계를 말하니 개념이 '모호하다'여야 맞아요. '분명한'은 반대예요 ←정답(부적절)
det.tip: the concept of self-actualization is vague = 개념이 모호하다(한계).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: love of power=권력욕 / fear of failure=실패에 대한 두려움 / freedom from fear=두려움으로부터의 자유 / need for praise=칭찬의 욕구
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞 'this feeling of security usually means protection and ______'가 단서예요. 안전 욕구(security)를 설명해요.

① love of power: 권력욕 — 안전감과 무관해요

② fear of failure: 실패에 대한 두려움 — 'protection(보호)'과 나란히 올 긍정적 안전 요소가 아니에요

③ freedom from fear: 두려움으로부터의 자유 — 보호와 함께 안전감의 핵심 요소 ←정답

④ need for praise: 칭찬의 욕구 — 존중 단계 욕구라 안전과 안 맞아요
det.tip: security = protection and freedom from fear.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: love and belonging=사랑과 소속 / food and shelter=음식과 주거 / truth and justice=진리와 정의 / power and wealth=권력과 부
det.analysis:
빈칸은 세 번째 단계예요. 바로 뒤에서 '가족·가정·집단·친구·팀'으로 충족한다고 설명해요.

① love and belonging: 사랑과 소속 — 가족·친구·팀으로 충족하는 세 번째 단계 ←정답

② food and shelter: 음식과 주거 — 1단계 생리적 욕구예요

③ truth and justice: 진리와 정의 — 최상위 자아실현 욕구예요

④ power and wealth: 권력과 부 — 본문에 없는 내용이에요
det.tip: families, friends, team으로 충족 → love and belonging.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 본문은 각 단계의 욕구를 충족한 뒤에야 다음 단계로 넘어갈 수 있다고 했어요.
det.analysis:
④ 본문 'satisfying the needs of each before being able to move on to the next'와 일치해요 ←정답

① 생리적 욕구는 'the bottom(맨 아래)'이라 가장 높은 단계가 아니에요

② 안전 욕구는 2단계, 사랑과 소속은 3단계라 안전 욕구가 더 하위예요

③ 'no evidence that every individual can reach it'이라 누구나 쉽게 도달하는 게 아니에요
det.tip: satisfy each before moving to the next = 충족 후 다음 단계.

ch: 생리적 욕구는 매슬로우 위계의 가장 높은 단계에 위치한다.
안전 욕구는 사랑과 소속 욕구보다 상위 단계이다.
자아실현은 누구나 쉽게 도달할 수 있는 단계이다.
각 단계의 욕구는 다음 단계로 넘어가기 전에 충족되어야 한다.

The most basic needs form the bottom of Maslow’s hierarchy and are referred to as physiological needs. Physiological needs include our needs for food and shelter. Unless these are satisfied, we cannot move to the next level, safety needs. We need to feel secure in our environment, and this feeling of security usually means protection and freedom from fear. The third level is the need for love and belonging. __________, as well as by joining and forming groups, making friends, and being part of a team. In the fourth level, the need for esteem refers to people’s need to be recognized. Here, they want to feel that others think highly of them; they may need praise and want to feel good about themselves. They may try to accomplish this by achieving set goals. Self-actualization, the fifth level, is the summit of Maslow’s hierarchy of needs. It is the quest to reach one’s full human potential. In this process people tend to have needs such as truth, justice, wisdom, and spiritual fulfillment. Despite the appealing logic of Maslow’s hierarchy, it seems to have some limits. Extensive research has suggested that there is little evidence for the ranking of levels and the argument of a definite hierarchy. Moreover, the concept of self-actualization is vague, and there’s no evidence to show that every individual can reach it. Maslow was the first psychologist to carry out academic research on human needs. He believed everybody should be encouraged to discover their vocations in life and endeavor to make life better. These are still important lessons today.
